children: Bikaji Foods International shares rose 7 per cent on Wednesday, snapping a two-day decline, after the company's Chief Operating Officer Manoj Verma maintained the company's sales and volume growth outlook for 2026-27, while flagging margin pressure due to higher raw material costs.
The stock rose nearly 10 per cent to Rs 607.50 apiece on the NSE during the day and settled 7 per cent higher.
The company maintained its expectation of mid-teens revenue growth in FY27, with volume growth guidance of 10-11 per cent, CNBC-TV18 reported, citing Verma.
He expects robust festive demand and strong growth in e-commerce sales to support volume growth.
However, Bikaji Foods expects its profit margins to contract by 100-150 basis points in FY27 as the company partially absorbs higher raw material costs.
"With all crude prices going up, all commodities going up, so margins - we feel that there would be a slip of about 100-150 basis points there," Verma said.

Raw material prices are expected to rise 6-7 per cent year-on-year, mainly due to higher edible oil prices and increased crude-linked packaging costs. The company has been able to pass on only 4.5-5 per cent of the cost increases to consumers, Verma said.
The company's export business is also facing headwinds from geopolitical challenges and container shortages, which have affected supply chains and increased freight costs nearly four times.

Bikaji Foods is also targeting the Western snacks category as part of its growth strategy. While traditional ethnic snacks remain its core business, the company sees an expansion opportunity in the larger Western snacks market.
Verma expects the Western snacks segment to grow 1.5 times faster than traditional snacks and account for 11-12 per cent of the company's overall business within the next two years.

title: Bikaji Foods shares snap 2-day fall to rise 7% as CEO maintains FY27 sales, volume outlook
